name: Lone Star Hiking Trail Corridor Dispersed Camping - Sam Houston National Forest

management_agency.name: U.S. Forest Service - Sam Houston Ranger District

rules_and_regulations.cost: 100% Free - No fees, no permits required for general dispersed primitive camping (outside general deer hunting season when primitive hunter camps apply)
rules_and_regulations.stay_limit: 14 consecutive days max stay within 30-day period
rules_and_regulations.guidelines: Dispersed primitive camping permitted throughout general national forest lands outside developed fee areas. Must be set back 100ft from trails and water bodies.

waste_disposal_rules.poop_disposal: Cathole method: dig 6 inches deep in sandy loam soil, 200 feet from streams and Lake Conroe drainages. Pack out toilet paper.
waste_disposal_rules.trash_policy: Strict Leave No Trace pack-it-in pack-it-out.

campfire_rules.firewood_policy: Gather dead and downed wood only within forest.
campfire_rules.safety_requirements: Clear pine straw 10 feet around fire ring. Extinguish cold to touch.
campfire_rules.seasonal_fire_bans: Obey Texas A&M Forest Service burn bans.

access_and_road_conditions.road_type: Paved state highway changing to unpaved gravel forest service roads (FS 215 / FS 208)
access_and_road_conditions.road_conditions: Flat gravel forest roads; side tracks can turn muddy after heavy Gulf rainstorms.
access_and_road_conditions.vehicle_recommendation: Normal low clearance front wheel drive car (easily accessible on main gravel forest roads in dry weather)

amenities: Lone Star National Recreation Trail Access

seasonal_weather_effects.spring: 65-80°F, pleasant pine forest climate, spring wildflowers.
seasonal_weather_effects.summer: Hot and humid (90-98°F), high insect activity, afternoon downpours.
seasonal_weather_effects.fall: Ideal camping season (65-78°F daytime, 45-55°F nights), dry forest roads.
seasonal_weather_effects.winter: Mild Texas winter (55-68°F daytime, 38-48°F nights), premier winter boondocking.

dangers_and_hazards: Venomous snakes: Copperheads, Cottonmouths, and Timber Rattlesnakes active in warm months
Mosquitoes and ticks in forest underbrush
Prescribed burns conducted by USFS during winter/spring

common_human_made_sounds: Distant highway hum on FM 1375 (2 miles away)

human_demographics_and_culture: Lone Star Trail backpackers, Houston area vanlifers, digital nomads, and local hunters.

spiritual_and_folklore_data.nature_spirits_and_mythological_lore: Bidai and Atakapa indigenous traditions honor the pine flatwoods and creek drainages of East Texas as ancient spirit lands.
spiritual_and_folklore_data.energetic_and_spiritual_features: Calming pine savannah grounding energy, mild winter climate, fast 5G connectivity.

nearby_hiking_trails.features: Continuous backpacking trail through East Texas pine forests and creek bridges

public_reviews_summary: Great free primitive camping spot in East Texas. Peaceful pine forests, easy driving access, and blazing fast 5G cell internet.
